clue.text: Yale gang, for a change, fail badly

indicators.note: the letters of the two words Yale gang are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A university gang tries something different and makes a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' is the anagram signal on YALE GANG.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who flops embarrassingly is said to have produced an egg, like a duck's zero score.

clue.text: Correspond after a duke gets fit

indicators.note: says the word for correspond comes after the a and the duke

parts.note: to correspond is to equate, match one thing to another

explanation.surface: A nobleman is made to match up and becomes fit for purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something fit for a task is sufficient, good enough for it.

clue.text: Classic western produced by RADA tutor?

definitions.meaning: the 1939 John Ford film starring John Wayne
RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art; a drama tutor trains people for the stage, hence a coach for the stage

explanation.surface: A cowboy film somehow turned out by an acting school teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical, marked by the question mark: a coach (trainer) for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the famous Ford western, and a playful description of a drama teacher.

clue.text: Extent of odds studied

definitions.meaning: the span or range something covers
in betting, the range of prices or margin that punters study

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs up how far the odds reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the reach of something, and the betting range between quoted prices.

clue.text: Rule clubs ignored after a while

indicators.note: says the letter for clubs is left out of the word for rule

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A rule about clubs gets overlooked after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning soon or presently, i.e. in a little while.

clue.text: To support energy, squeeze in very strong coffee

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below, so it follows the energy letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: says the word for squeeze goes inside the word for very

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
to press is to squeeze

explanation.surface: Advice to squeeze a powerful coffee in for an energy boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, concentrated coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Group inside enjoys terrific shellfish

indicators.note: the run of letters grouped inside the phrase enjoys terrific gives the hidden word

explanation.surface: A group of people inside is having a terrific time.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a bivalve mollusc eaten raw, one kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Ship — clipper, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a small fast single-masted sailing vessel
a tool that clips, such as shears, is something that cuts

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a type of boat, and an instrument for cutting, which a clipper exemplifies.

clue.text: Difficult at college being short of money

parts.note: hard means difficult
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A struggling student finds college life tough without funds.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for being broke or lacking cash.

clue.text: Facing plot after work, work over

indicators.note: says the plot comes after the works

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: means the second work is turned back to front

parts.note: OP again, short for opus
a site is a plot of land

explanation.surface: Someone faces more scheming after a job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: facing as in across from, the house facing the church.

clue.text: Famous guitarist with his group, one presiding over celebrations

parts.note: Brian May, lead guitarist of the rock band
Queen, the band Brian May played in

explanation.surface: A rock star and his band preside over a big party.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl crowned to reign over traditional May Day festivities in English villages.

clue.text: Time for a coffee in the Spanish fair

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even means fair, as in an even contest

explanation.surface: Taking a coffee break at a fair in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mid-morning snack is called elevenses, taken around this hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour of the British mid-morning break for a hot drink.

clue.text: Anyway, don't contemplate so much

definitions.meaning: an instruction to look at or consider things less, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adverb meaning in any case, and the split reading of considering a smaller amount.

clue.text: Faux pas made by enfant terrible blowing top

indicators.note: losing temper, read as losing the top letter of the word

parts.note: an unruly person, a terror

explanation.surface: A tantrum-throwing brat commits a social gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a faux pas is a social blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Area round capital no longer rated badly

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase no longer rated are put together poorly, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A district near the capital has slipped down the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative region comprising the British capital and its surrounding boroughs.

clue.text: Count late manoeuvring as revealing

parts.note: to tell is to count, as a bank teller does

indicators.note: the word late is moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An aristocrat arriving late gives himself away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a giveaway sign is revealing, betraying something hidden.

clue.text: Daughter put on excellent meaty spread

indicators.note: in a down answer the daughter's letter sits on top of the word for excellent

parts.note: ripping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A daughter puts on a fine meat feast.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef dripping is fat from roasting meat, spread on bread in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat collected from roasting meat, eaten spread on toast.

clue.text: Barking canine with us, a source of irritation

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters of canine and us are jumbled

explanation.surface: A yapping dog living with us is an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a pest or bother is something that irritates.

clue.text: Primate's word of disapproval during Prohibition

indicators.note: places the jeer inside the word for prohibition

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
boo is shouted in disapproval

explanation.surface: An archbishop speaks out against the Prohibition era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, but here it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a large African monkey, one of the primates.

clue.text: Page about marvellous small house

parts.note: re means about, concerning
fab is short for fabulous, marvellous

explanation.surface: A page written about a wonderful little house.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated building, typically a small single-storey dwelling put up after the war.

clue.text: Try sailing at sea — it could make you hoarse

indicators.note: confused, so the letters of try sailing are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shouting into the wind while sailing could cost you your voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box, which leaves the sufferer croaky.

clue.text: Sickness in Ghana? Use antibiotics

indicators.note: the letters run inside the phrase Ghana use antibiotics

explanation.surface: A traveller with an illness in West Africa is told to take medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: queasiness or feeling sick to the stomach.

clue.text: Police unit using bad PR a lot

indicators.note: the letters of PR a lot are put in a bad order, rearranged

explanation.surface: The police force relies heavily on poor publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of officers sent round an area to keep watch.

clue.text: Dishonest behaviour in dreadful piece of drama

parts.note: foul means dreadful, awful
a play is a dramatic work

explanation.surface: Cheating occurs in an awful stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for cheating or crime, originally from unfair conduct in sport.

clue.text: Half a century in Rome inhabiting big residence

indicators.note: the Roman fifty lives inside the word for big

parts.note: fat means big
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty years in Rome spent living in a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A home on one floor of a building, an apartment.

clue.text: One with dimples that may get hooked on a course

definitions.text: One with dimples that may get hooked on a course

parts.words: One with dimples that may get hooked on a course
parts.note: suggests a dimpled person getting caught up on a course of study, but means a dimpled sphere that is hit with a hook shot on the links

explanation.walkthrough: A hook is a shot curving sharply left, and the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The small dimpled sphere used in a round of golf, which is struck off line by a hook.

clue.text: Pleasant accompanying English university girl

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A pleasant girl accompanies an English student.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, the usual crossword meaning of girl.

clue.text: While not present at work, a bishop posted one article

parts.note: in means at work, as in in the office
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
sent means posted
I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bishop sends a letter from the office during someone's absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin legal phrase for something done when the person concerned is absent.
